newsitem.title: USA: Capstead sees higher Q1 EPS, dividend.
newsitem.headline: Capstead sees higher Q1 EPS, dividend.

text.p: Capstead Mortgage Corp said Tuesday it is confident that its earnings per share and common dividend will increase in 1997's first quarter, thanks to the restructuring of its investment portfolio and improving results from mortgage servicing in 1996.
Unless there is a dramatic change in interest rates, the company said it expects the common dividend to continue to grow throughout 1997.

"From the third to the fourth quarter in 1996, the dividend increased from $0.55 to $0.565," Andrew Jacobs, Capstead's senior vice president and treasurer, said in a telephone interview."I think that kind of increase is a reasonable expectation for the first quarter."
"Our dividend in the fourth quarter was indicative of our earnings per share," Jacobs said. "If our dividend in the first quarter is higher, it follows that our earnings will be higher as well."
Capstead today reported diluted earnings per share for the fourth quarter rose to $0.56 from $0.36 in the year-ago period.
In its earnings release Capstead said its mortgage servicing portfolio continues to be productive and the company expects profits from its servicing business to grow by about 10 percent during 1997.
Jacobs said 1996 earnings from mortgage servicing accounted for $49.1 million out the company's total income of $127.2 million.

The company said in its earnings statement it has committed to purchase an additional $4.2 billion in mortgage servicing rights with a weighted average interest rate of 7.67 percent, which should increase the servicing portfolio to more than $39 billion by the end of February, 1997.

The company also said it expects to increase income from subservicing by five percent during 1997, as a result of a previously announced subservicing arrangement with a large national mortgage originator, whereby Capstead services single family mortgage loans for the originator.
Jacobs declined to name the mortgage originator, saying the company is contractually prohibited from doing so.
The company's stock was up 5/8 at 24-1/4 in early afternoon trading.
